stage: STAGE 8.13 SATELLITE CLOUD INFORMATION FEASIBILITY AUDIT

primary_decision.verdict_summary: No satellite-cloud candidate identified in the current GPT/AI assistant research round was demonstrated to satisfy all required conditions for a POLARIS forecasting experiment: causal availability, empirical coverage, spatial representativeness, information novelty beyond the frozen Stage 8.1 feature set, and a clearly testable operational pathway.

gpt_proposals.audit_verdict: UNVERIFIED OPERATIONAL PATHWAY / HIGH VZA GEOMETRY
gpt_proposals.reasoning: High calculated Satellite Viewing Zenith Angle (VZA ≈ 76.54° at 68.36°N) induces calculated geometric distortion and horizontal parallax shifts (>20.9 km for 5 km cloud tops). Solar optical channels (COT/CER) are unavailable during polar night (SZA > 84°), though thermal IR phase remains available. Standard publication latency exceeds t0. Stage 8.9A previously classified geostationary products as not feasible for Nuolja.

gpt_proposals.audit_verdict: UNVERIFIED OPERATIONAL PRODUCT FOR BENCHMARK HORIZON
gpt_proposals.reasoning: Available candidate ML cloud-nowcasting products were not verified to provide a causally available, 2024-reconstructable operational product covering the full H1-H24 benchmark horizon at Nuolja.

ai_proposals.reasoning: Existing POLARIS evidence does not establish a sufficiently novel, causally available, and operationally representative satellite cloud-motion route for the current benchmark. Stage 8.5's MEPS spatial-advection rejection cannot by itself be generalized to all satellite cloud-motion methods, but no operational, causally available satellite cloud-motion product was demonstrated.
